correctness.rationale: On compact invariant support in the positive quadrant, log P and log N are bounded and the two multiplicative factors are positive. Invariance gives zero integrals of log(P_next/P) and log(N_next/N). Strict log Jensen gives exp(J_P)=1+h(E N-m), and exp(J_N)=1+(h/epsilon)(E[g(N)/(1+fP)]-E P). Equality in J_P forces N=m almost surely; invariance and prey update force P=P_* uniquely, so every nontrivial invariant measure has E N>m and positive mass N<m,N>m. Completing g square gives E P< (1-theta)²/4. Computation of 0.2025 and 0.038025 is exact decimal arithmetic. No existence of chaotic measures or invariant curves proved.
residual_risks: Strictness relies on uniquely positive equilibrium and bounded integrable logarithms.
